intervals.quote: The proposed MOLLER experiment will improve on this result by a factor of five

intervals.label: construction
intervals.locator: APS April Meeting 2024 abstract (6 Apr 2024); APS 2025: "now in its construction phase"; APS 2026: assembly to finish late 2026; JLab Hall A Feb 2026: installation started
intervals.note: April 2024 is the earliest source found stating that the experiment is under construction; construction may have begun earlier. Funding: DOE (MIE), NSF, CFI/RM (APS 2025 talk).
intervals.quote: The experiment is currently in the construction and prototype testing phase

intervals.label: physics running (planned)
intervals.locator: JLab Hall A update, February 2026, conclusion slide; APS 2025 talk: "Ready for physics in early 2027."
intervals.note: Schedule, not an event: "Will start running in 2027 for 3 years"; the end year is the start plus the stated three years. Earlier talks gave 2025/2026 targets, so the schedule has slipped.
intervals.quote: MOLLER installation is in progress. Will start running in 2027 for 3 years.

placements.locator: JLab Hall A update, February 2026, MOLLER slide
placements.note: Installation of the apparatus in Hall A began (SBS deinstallation completed); the placement start is that installation, not data taking.
placements.quote: SBS Deinstallation completed. Installation has started.

subsystems.quote: The MOLLER experiment has 11 major subsystems, including the target, spectrometer and collimators, the main detectors and several types of auxilliary detectors.
subsystems.value: 11 major subsystems including target, spectrometer and collimators, main detectors and auxiliary detectors

summary.plain: The apparatus being installed in Hall A: a long liquid-hydrogen target, two sets of toroidal magnets that focus scattered electrons into a ring, and quartz detectors that measure the light they produce.
summary.technical: MOLLER apparatus with 11 major subsystems: liquid-hydrogen target, toroidal spectrometer and collimators focusing Møller electrons to a ring about 30 m downstream, fused-silica Cherenkov main detectors, beam monitors, polarimetry (two independent polarimeters), tracking detectors for Q^2 calibration and auxiliary background detectors.

technology.quote: The MOLLER experiment has 11 major subsystems, including the target, spectrometer and collimators, the main detectors and several types of auxilliary detectors.
technology.value: Toroidal-magnet spectrometer with fused-silica Cherenkov detectors measuring the integrated Møller-electron flux per beam-helicity state
